NEEDS_FIX: YES
<assessment>The sources show the same building from near-front and front-right: stepped white screened volumes, a central peaked vertical spine with small windows, deep recesses, red columns and elevated decks, lower glazed rooms, upper-right corner glazing, red folded roof elements, external stairs and a white ramp. Shared landmarks establish their connections; no dimensions are supplied, and rear geometry remains uncertain. CURRENT retains this general arrangement, but the upper-left recess, roof folds and circulation geometry differ substantially. Screenshots cannot establish watertight joints or concealed connections.</assessment>
<issue priority="1" view="front">problem: The upper-left recess has become an almost empty opening with an exposed straight stair. SOURCE 1 shows a substantial white-sided diagonal circulation element beneath the small red fold, bounded above by a deep screened fascia. CURRENT loses that enclosure and changes the opening's silhouette.
action: Locally restore the visible white stair-side enclosure and upper screened fascia depth; adjust the flight and landing positions against both source angles while preserving the lower-left glazed bays.</issue>
<issue priority="2" view="roof">problem: The large red roof fold presents a thin diagonal blade in CURRENT's near-front view and a broad projecting triangle in its front-right view. The sources show a broad, near-upright red face beside the central spine, descending toward connected lower folds within the right screened enclosure.
action: Adjust the existing fold's orientation, vertices and connections to reproduce its visible face and descending profile in both source angles. Preserve the small left red fold; hidden roof topology is unverified.</issue>
<issue priority="3" view="right">problem: CURRENT's white ramp reads as a narrow straight trough, whereas SOURCE 2 shows a broad rising route with a return near the central support. The lower glazed circulation also lacks the source's clearly connected diagonal red stair and landing arrangement.
action: Locally correct the ramp width, return and landing connection, then align the lower stair flights with the glazed deck. Verify actual landing contacts and clearances rather than relying on projected overlaps.</issue>
<keep>
The two stacked glazed openings at the far-left edge, separated by a red floor band.
The small rectangular windows arranged vertically on the central spine.
The red material assignment of the exposed columns and elevated deck edges.
</keep>

events.text:
NEEDS_FIX: YES
<assessment>SOURCE1 is a near-frontal ground view; SOURCE2 looks along the right flank. Shared landmarks identify the same building: stepped white perforated enclosures, a narrow central strip of small windows, two stacked left glazing bays, a deep right recess with corner glazing and tall red columns, red folded rooftop surfaces, elevated glazed rooms, and external stairs and a pale ramp. CURRENT retains these broad landmarks, but its upper enclosure silhouette and circulation assemblies differ substantially. The source-matched views are elevated relative to the photographs, so perspective alone cannot establish exact dimensions. Rear geometry, concealed roof extents and structural joints remain uncertain; screenshots cannot verify actual geometric attachment.</assessment>
<issue priority="1" view="right">problem: SOURCE2 shows a substantial screened right-hand enclosure continuing below the corner glazing and framing the deep recess. CURRENT10 instead exposes a hanging glazed box with a plain white lower face beneath a comparatively shallow upper screen band. This changes the principal volume and recess boundaries.
action: Locally extend and reshape the visible right-side enclosure and its lower return to match SOURCE2, retaining the recessed glazing where its placement agrees. Align screen, soffit and glazing edges at their intended junctions; preserve the open recess.</issue>
<issue priority="2" view="roof">problem: Both sources show pronounced peaked and sloping white screen outlines around the red folded rooftop geometry. CURRENT9–10 largely flatten these into horizontal rims, with only a small central peak. CURRENT also presents the red assembly mainly as an upright fin and narrow rising strip rather than the broad folded surface visible in SOURCE1.
action: Adjust the affected screen crest profiles and visible red fold widths, slopes and connections using both source angles. Limit changes to source-visible portions; do not invent concealed roof geometry.</issue>
<issue priority="3" view="front">problem: The sources show substantial red stair flights and landings, plus a broad pale ramp with a turning or curved boundary at ground level. CURRENT9–10 reduce these to narrow exposed flights and a straight channel-like ramp, altering the lower silhouette and circulation connections.
action: Patch the visible stair widths, solid side/underside profiles and landing connections, then reshape the ramp’s visible boundary and approach to match the sources. Verify continuous connections and clearances at the elevated deck rather than relying on overlapping faces.</issue>
<keep>Two stacked glazed bays at the left opening, separated by a red horizontal floor edge.
The vertical arrangement of three small rectangular openings on the narrow central front strip.</keep>
